title: What Counts As A Humanities Dataset?
thesis: A humanities dataset becomes analytically useful when access, rights, metadata structure, time depth, and coverage bias are legible together.

readyNowCandidates.name: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API
readyNowCandidates.starterQuestion: What acquisition, creation-date, and department patterns appear in open museum data?
readyNowCandidates.qualityRisk: One museum collection is analytically rich but institution-specific.

readyNowCandidates.name: Wikidata
readyNowCandidates.starterQuestion: How are authors, artworks, institutions, languages, and movements connected in public linked data?
readyNowCandidates.qualityRisk: Wikidata reflects contributor attention and ontology gaps.

readyNowCandidates.name: Library of Congress Digital Collections
readyNowCandidates.starterQuestion: Which subjects, formats, and eras dominate digitized public collections?
readyNowCandidates.qualityRisk: Collection metadata reflects digitization and cataloging priorities.

readyNowCandidates.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art Collection API
readyNowCandidates.starterQuestion: How do object dates, geographies, departments, and acquisition histories differ across the Met collection?
readyNowCandidates.qualityRisk: Collection API records vary in completeness and public-domain image availability.

readyNowCandidates.name: Open Syllabus
readyNowCandidates.starterQuestion: Which works and authors appear in syllabi across institutions, fields, and time?
readyNowCandidates.qualityRisk: Public access and export terms need explicit review before automated collection.

readyNowCandidates.name: Project Gutenberg
readyNowCandidates.starterQuestion: How do genres, publication dates, and author cohorts shape public-domain literary corpora?
readyNowCandidates.qualityRisk: Public-domain availability is not the same as literary representativeness.

editorialFrame: Use the registry as a research-agenda essay, not as a definitive list of all humanities datasets.
Show that dataset readiness is multidimensional: access, rights, structure, time depth, entity richness, and normalization burden.
Treat ready-now as ready for source-probed experimentation, not as representative of culture.
Point directly to the Cleveland study as the first launched example from the registry.
publicClaimChecklist: Say the registry probes 15 candidate corpora, not the whole humanities data universe.
Mention 11 accessible candidates and 6 ready-now candidates.
Separate public availability from cultural representativeness.
Do not imply API richness means interpretive neutrality.
Include licensing and redistribution caveats before recommending derivative datasets.
Point readers to 5 generated study specs as next experiments, not final results.
copyeditNotes: Lead with the question: what makes a pile of cultural material become a usable humanities dataset?
Use the ranked candidates to make the method concrete.
Keep examples diverse across museums, linked data, libraries, teaching, and books.
End with a short publication roadmap from registry to study spec to essay.
